text:
emily: FYI I pushed a first-pass replay harness for production traces to the repo. Goal: apples-to-apples perf comparisons for kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV-cache behavior. Need help defining anonymization + sampling + parity checks. PR: https://redwood-internal/pull/2345 :eyes:

sam: nice. does the harness enforce deterministic seeds for kernel selection and batching?

emily: it exposes --seed and docs mention forcing REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE, but we haven't locked all envs yet. want to list required pins.

kavi: important: KV cache reuse causes divergence if replay doesn't mimic client prefix behavior. two quick rules: 1) either reset KV between replays or 2) faithfully replay client prefix+streaming order. we tried both and saw different outcomes.

kavi: also kernel selection currently depends on heuristics (sequence length distribution + device properties). for apples-to-apples you must set REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=<kernel-name> or set REDWOOD_KERNEL_SEED to make selection deterministic across hosts.

nate: sampling config proposal (use this to generate small test sets from huge traces):
```json
{
  "sample_rate": 0.01,
  "min_samples": 10000,
  "stratify_by": ["seq_len_bucket","model_name","route"]
}
```

emily: anonymization rules I used: drop user ids, map emails->user<N>, strip URL query params, replace quoted blocks > 200 chars with <REDACTED>. keep token counts and conversation boundaries. pseudo: `text = re.sub(email_re, lambda m: "user"+hash(m.group()), text)`

zara: for parity we need two orthogonal checks: 1) functional parity (token-level outputs or stable hash of samplable outputs) 2) perf parity (latency + hardware counters). example metrics: token_match_ratio, logits_mse, p50/p95 latency diff.

zara: small run results I posted from the first 2k-sample test: token_match_ratio=99.87%, logits_mse=0.0012, latency_p50=18ms (baseline 17.5ms), latency_p95=73ms (baseline 71ms). those deltas are acceptable for now but worth tracking as regressions.

sam: where did the 0.13% mismatch come from? numeric nondeterminism or a bug?

kavi: 0.13% came from a couple sources: different kernel rounding in quantized matmuls + KV cache warmup ordering (streaming vs batch order). we saw most mismatches concentrated on long-context samples.

emily: harness includes a `parity-report` mode that outputs: token hashes per-step, logits MSE per-sample, and a reproducible failure case collector. example run command: `./replay --trace s3://redwood-prod/traces/2026-03-01 --sample-config sample.json --anonymize-config anon.json --seed 42 --force-kernel fused-attn-v2 --parity-output ./out`

infra-bot: replay-runner started (job id r-20260318-042). logs: https://internal-logs/replay/r-20260318-042

nate: small note on determinism: pin drivers and CuDNN/cuBLAS versions; different driver microcode can flip low-bit results and cascade. we should record `nvidia-smi --query` and `python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__)"` into the run metadata.

kavi: add to environment checklist: MODEL_GIT_SHA, MODEL_QUANT_PROFILE, REDWOOD_KERNEL_* flags, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, GPU_DRIVER_HASH. also note CPU affinity and mem-bind for consistent host noise.

sam: for KV cache testing: we should include a mode that replays exact arrival timestamps (to verify batching heuristics) vs an idealized mode that uses fixed inter-arrival times.

emily: yes. current harness has two clocks: `--replay-time` (honor original timestamps) and `--uniform-time` (fixed IAT). comparing both exposes batching and jitter effects.

zara: threshold proposal for alerts: token_match_ratio < 99.5% -> fail, logits_mse > 0.005 -> investigate, latency_p95 delta > +10% -> fail. open to adjusting but want automated gating.

emily: next steps: 1) run 10k stratified samples with seed=42, kernel forced to fused-attn-v2, 3 repeats; 2) collect parity reports and failing-case corpus; 3) compare kernel variants (fused-attn-v1 vs v2) on same sample. volunteers?

kavi: I can run kernel comparison on a small cluster today.

sam: I'll own the anonymization review and add a quick fuzz test that ensures PII is removed.

emily: thanks. I'll update the PR with the env checklist and the parity thresholds. tagging @eng-sre for any infra quota needs. :thumbsup:
